prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single universally “best” roofer — the best one for you depends on your location in Denver, your roof type, insurance needs, and whether you want a low-cost repair or a manufacturer-certified replacement. I can help find well-rated local contractors if you give your ZIP code or address. Meanwhile, here’s how to find and pick the best roofer for hail damage.

What to look for in a hail-damage roofer
- Insurance & licensing: Contractor carries general liability and workers’ comp; verify policy numbers. Check local registrations.
- Hail/insurance experience: Has experience working with insurance claims and adjusters.
- Manufacturer certification: Certified by shingle manufacturers (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning) if you want to preserve/or get enhanced warranties.
- Local reputation: Strong, recent Google/Yelp/Angi reviews and good BBB rating.
- Written warranty: Clear workmanship warranty plus manufacturer shingle warranty options.
- Transparent estimates: Itemized, explains what’s covered vs. excluded, identifies secondary issues (ice/water, underlayment).
- Proper permits & disposal: Will pull required city/county permits and remove old roofing debris responsibly.
- References & portfolio: Can provide recent local references and photos from hail jobs.

Immediate steps after hail
1. Document damage: Take photos from ground and of gutters, siding, vents, vehicles.
2. Avoid repairs by storm-chasers: Don’t sign high-pressure contracts from contractors who just arrived after the storm without local references.
3. Contact your insurer: Report claim and ask about preferred vs. any certified contractors.
4. Get at least 3 written estimates: Compare scopes, materials, pricing and warranty.
5. Verify everything in writing before work begins.

Key questions to ask contractors
- How long have you been doing hail repairs in Denver?
- Can you provide proof of insurance and license/registration?
- Are you a certified installer for (manufacturer)?
- Will you handle permits and disposal?
- How do you work with my insurance company — will you meet the adjuster?
- What is included in the estimate and what’s excluded?
- What warranties do you provide (workmanship & materials)?
- Can you provide recent local references and photos of completed hail jobs?
- Do you use subcontractors? If so, are they insured?

Red flags
- High-pressure “sign today” tactics or demand for full payment upfront.
- No written estimate or vague scope.
- No local references or mostly 1–2-star reviews.
- Unwillingness to provide insurance certificate or lien waivers.
- Requests to have insurance check pay contractor directly without your approval.

Where to search reputable Denver roofers
- Google Maps (filter by reviews)
- Angi / HomeAdvisor
- Yelp
- BBB (check complaints/resolutions)
- Manufacturer websites for certified installers (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning)
- Local Facebook community pages or Nextdoor for neighborhood recommendations

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated Denver roofers near you (share ZIP code)
- Provide a short list of vetted contractors with links to reviews and questions to ask each
- Help draft an email or phone script to request estimates
